title: iPhone connectivity issues
body:
### What is the issue?

iPhone unable to access internet/Tailscale nodes until service is toggled on then off again. 

### Steps to reproduce

On my home WiFi. Tailscale set as connect on demand to everything except my home WiFi. 

Leave home. 
Connection works for 4 minutes.
Connection does not work.
Toggle Tailscale off/on.
Connection fixed. 

Note in this example I am a passenger in a car. 

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

No. I was advised by Andrea a fix was in the TestFlight build, so I have switched over. The issue still persists. 

### OS

iOS

### OS version

17.2.1

### Tailscale version

1.57.44

### Other software

Nothing

### Bug report

BUG-36799cb0c303eb03303c3cddf7f557882de9d9c19e657e0022895fff872714d7-20240111104610Z-416864e991d8e86d

@participant3 In the Tailscale iOS app, tap on your avatar then tap Bug Report and copy the bug marker displayed there.

Each of the bug reports in this thread have reported DNS issues shortly before the report was generated.
* wg: IPv4 packet with disallowed source address from [x]
* dns udp query: context deadline exceeded

This would be a different issue from the fix we shipped in 1.58. I'll add the correct labels and we'll take a closer look and will update this issue once we have more to share.

comments.body:
> @participant2 I suspect your issue could be related to a setting or firewall policing `tailscale0` on your DNS resolver node. When your phone switched from wifi to cellular I see the following error after a few moments:
> 

I am not quite sure which DNS you are reffering to here. In participant10 I have two DNS-servers defined; 192.168.103.11 and 192.168.103.10. On the exit-node I am using, which has IP 192.168.0.46, those two dns-servers are 100% available. If the tailscale0 interface is using the default gateway, which is 192.168.0.1, it should have not problems reaching the DNS-servers. There are no blocks in my firewall for that.

I have added an explicit route for the 192.168.103.0/24 network incase the participant10 network interface doesn't understand the default gateway somehow... I'll update if there are any changes.

Also, it doesn't make sense that there would be some kind of block on my end. In that case it wouldn't work to simply disconnect and reconnect to participant10 to get it to work... which it does.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body: Sorry for the frustration. We have been actively fixing many DNS issues related to network transitions, you can see that in the changelog. It is just a very hard problem, with many hard-to-hit edge cases, and it is often impossible for engineers to repro reliably, so coming up with a good fix that fixes the problem for _everyone_ is hard. @participant11 is slated to look into https://github.com/participant10/participant10/issues/12352 next week, which appears to be the same issue as what you're experiencing (based on your diagnostics it appears you're also using DNS over HTTPS).

comments.author: participant9
comments.body: @participant2 Diagnostics from your tailnet and your client indicate there are no network transitions happening. The issue you're experiencing is not the issue originally mentioned in this thread. The client is hitting timeouts reaching the DNS server you specified on your tailnet. Support will reach out to you privately with troubleshooting steps as it appears a misconfiguration is causing this and I don't want to publish details about your tailnet configuration in a public thread.
